warningSignalRace.title: Does the warning arrive first?
warningSignalRace.subtitle: An alarm is only an alarm if it beats the herbivore to the neighbour.
warningSignalRace.aria: A signal crossing soil between an attacked plant and its neighbour, reaching {reach} of a {distance} gap before the deadline

hint.inTime: The warning lands before the attack does — so the neighbour has its defences up when the aphids arrive. Notice how small the gap has to be for this to work.
hint.tooLate: The alarm is still crawling through the soil when the herbivore arrives. The signal is real; over this distance it is simply too slow to be a warning.

warningSignalRace.deadlineSlider: Time before the herbivore reaches the neighbour

isotopeTracerAudit.title: Build the experiment, earn the claim
isotopeTracerAudit.subtitle: Switch each control on and see which sentence the design lets you write.
isotopeTracerAudit.aria: An isotope-tracing experiment with {n} of {total} controls in place, and the strongest claim it supports
isotopeTracerAudit.routeLabel: shared soil and the fungal link between the root systems
isotopeTracerAudit.meshMarker: mesh: cuts hyphae, passes soil water
isotopeTracerAudit.claimNote: The design cannot support anything above this
isotopeTracerAudit.controlsNote: Each one closes a different escape route

confound.donorUnknown: With one label you can find the isotope in the receiver and still not know which plant it started in. Nothing can be claimed until the donor is distinguishable.
confound.soilLeak: Carbon reached the receiver — but sugars leak from roots into soil and neighbours take them up independently. Without a barrier, the fungal route is one explanation among several.
confound.noGradient: The mesh rules out the soil, so the link really did carry it. What the design still cannot show is direction: nothing here says the flow followed anyone's need.
confound.kinUntested: This is what Simard's design earned — net flow running down a shading gradient, from the sunlit tree toward the struggling one. The kin claim is not tested and cannot be inferred.
confound.potArtifact: Related seedlings in pots can show a kin effect that pots create. Continuous wild forest is where the claim has to hold, and where it has almost never been attempted.
confound.none: Every escape route closed — and this is precisely the design forest ecology has essentially never run. The 2023 review found no field evidence for the kin claim at all, which is why it stays a hypothesis.

dualIsotope.name: Two distinguishable labels
dualIsotope.detail: Feed each species a different carbon isotope so any molecule found can be traced to the plant it started in.

meshBarrier.name: Hyphae-severing mesh
meshBarrier.detail: A fine barrier that cuts the fungal threads while still letting soil water through, so the two routes can be told apart.

sourceSink.name: A shading gradient
sourceSink.detail: Shade the receiver so it cannot photosynthesise, creating the source-to-sink difference that makes direction meaningful.

kinDesign.name: Related receivers
kinDesign.detail: Compare seedlings related to the donor against strangers — the only way the mother-tree claim becomes testable at all.

wildForest.name: Continuous wild forest
wildForest.detail: Run it in real forest soil with mapped fungal individuals, not pots, so the result speaks for the ecosystem.

latencyHorizon.title: How much of a moon can answer in time?
latencyHorizon.subtitle: Capacity says how much crosses. Latency says how much of the planet is even in reach.
latencyHorizon.aria: A disc of Pandora with the reachable region glowing: a signal reaches {reach} within the deadline, dividing the moon into {regions} regions

hint.whole: At this speed and this deadline the whole moon is inside one horizon — every part of the network can answer every other part in time. This is what it takes for a planet to act as one.
hint.fragmented: The moon breaks into roughly {n} regions that cannot reach each other inside the deadline. Each is coherent; none of them can coordinate with the rest. A planetary network, but not a planetary moment.

latencyHorizon.crossingNote: Straight line, halfway around the moon — the floor, not the real delay
latencyHorizon.regionsLabel: Regions in reach of each other
latencyHorizon.regionsNote: How many separate horizons the moon holds
latencyHorizon.speedNote: Electrochemical signalling spans about 1 m/s in bare fibres to {max} m/s in the fattest insulated ones. Nothing biological is known to go faster, so the whole slider is the real envelope.

regenerationRace.title: Burning against regrowth
regenerationRace.subtitle: Resilience is not armour. It is a rate — and a rate can be outrun.
regenerationRace.aria: A trajectory of how much of the network is still standing over two centuries, ending at {pct} percent: {verdict}

hint.shattered: Burning outpaces reseeding, the standing network slides to the critical density, and in year {year} the connected whole does not dim — it shatters into islands in a single step.
hint.holding: Reseeding keeps up. The forest carries a permanent scar — it levels off around {pct}% of what it was — and stays one connected network the whole way.

regenerationRace.regrowNote: Reseeding is done by the forest that survives, so it slows as the network shrinks — which is why the losing side of this race accelerates instead of levelling out.
